messages:
maria.g: FYI we have a P2 from Acme — their internal NLB target group shows targets UNHEALTHY intermittently and customers see 502s. They say traffic to envoy sometimes fails health checks.
customer-ops: Escalation ticket attached:  #12345 — customer notes it started after they added a network inspection appliance in their VPC.
samir: Can you paste the NLB health check config and a short tcpdump from the target while the check happens?
mar ia.g: Config: protocol=TCP, port=443, interval=10, timeout=5, healthy=2, unhealthy=2. Targets are Envoy listeners doing TLS termination. tcpdump snippet from target when probe fails:
```
14:22:03.123456 IP 10.0.2.18.54321 > 10.0.4.22.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
14:22:03.123456 IP 10.0.4.22.443 > 10.0.2.18.54321: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 12346, win 0
```
maria.g: No TLS ClientHello shows up — the connection gets RST right away. When probe passes we do see TLS, but that is rare.
alex: RST from the target implies something in the stack is closing, or a proxy in path is rejecting the handshake.
samir: They mentioned a "network inspection appliance" — is it doing TLS intercept or a transparent proxy that expects HTTP(S) negotiation? If it injects or terminates TLS it could break a bare TCP healthcheck to a TLS-listening process.
signe: Also check that the inspection appliance isn't configured to terminate on port 443 and then forward with a different protocol. If the appliance sends a TCP reset for unknown flows that aren't completion of a TLS handshake, that explains the immediate RST.
maria.g: Good call. Customer confirms the appliance is doing selective TLS inspection and will intercept plaintext TCP 443 unless it sees a proper SNI/host header. Health checks are raw TCP so they don't include SNI.
alex: Right — TCP health check won't send TLS ClientHello so inspection appliance treats it as suspicious and kills the flow. That matches RST. Two quick options:
- Make the NLB health check use HTTPS (application-level) so it sends a ClientHello / Host and SNI, or an HTTP GET to path /health.
- Or add a bypass rule on the inspection appliance for the NLB nodes' IP range so healthchecks pass through unmodified and reach Envoy.
samir: If we change to HTTPS health checks, we need to ensure target Envoy serves a plain HTTPS health endpoint that returns 200 w/o requiring client certs. Also set the Host header to match the server_name used by Envoy.
signe: Another option — use a TCP health check to a dedicated health endpoint port that the inspection appliance doesn't intercept. Many users put a nonstandard port (e.g., 15020) for internal health checks.
maria.g: Customer prefers not to open extra ports. They're going to try HTTPS health check first. I'll suggest a minimal Envoy listener route that responds on /redwood-hc with 200 and accepts only local health probes.
customer-ops: Customer will test in the next hour and update.
maria.g: Quick repro steps I gave them:
1) On a test target: curl -vk --resolve "svc.test:443:127.0.0.1" https://svc.test/redwood-hc --header "Host: svc.test"
2) Check tcpdump for ClientHello from the NLB node ip during hc: `tcpdump -nni any port 443 and host 10.0.2.18`
3) If no ClientHello appears, create bypass rule for the NLB node range 10.0.2.0/24 on the inspection appliance.
alex: Also verify SGs/NACLs allow the healthcheck source range — but since we see SYN from 10.0.2.18 the SG is fine.
samir: After customer switches to HTTPS hc, ensure the health check TLS handshake sends SNI. AWS/ALB health checks support setting Host header, and with NLB+TLS you might need to configure TLS health checks via target group type "instance" + hc protocol HTTPS. Confirm in their console.
maria.g: Update: customer switched target-group hc to HTTPS w/ Host=svc.test and path=/redwood-hc. Tests pass, targets go HEALTHY within 30s. They said the inspection appliance now allows the flow because it sees proper TLS.
signe: Nice. Recommend long-term: either keep HTTPS hc or add bypass for the appliance for the LB node IP range. Also consider dedicated health port if they want purely TCP checks.
maria.g: Marking incident resolved from our side. I'll add notes to the ticket: root cause: TLS-intercepting inspection appliance terminated raw TCP health checks (no ClientHello) and reset flows. Mitigation: use HTTPS health check with Host/SNI or bypass appliance for LB healthchecks. :white_check_mark:
customer-ops: Customer confirmed production traffic unaffected after change and will roll the hc update to all envs tomorrow. Closing ticket.
devops-bot: Deployment note — healthcheck change applied to tg svc-test-hc by maria.g at 2026-03-16T14:55:00Z
